quests.instruction: Mia bites into a crunchy apple at lunchtime. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: Picture what your mouth and teeth are busy with at lunchtime.
quests.explanation: Eat means to take food into your mouth, chew it and swallow it. Drink is the word for liquids.
quests.funFact: Your front teeth cut food and your back teeth grind it.

quests.instruction: Tom is very thirsty and picks up a glass of cold milk. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: A glass is made for liquids, not for chewing.
quests.explanation: Drink means to swallow a liquid. We drink milk, water and juice.
quests.funFact: More than half of your body is water, which is why you need to drink every day.

quests.instruction: It is dark, and Anu is lying in bed with her eyes closed. What is she doing?
quests.hint: The room is quiet and her eyes are shut.
quests.explanation: Sleep means to rest with your eyes closed and your mind quiet, usually at night.
quests.funFact: Children aged six to twelve usually need about nine to twelve hours of sleep.

quests.instruction: The school bell is about to ring, so Ravi moves fast on his feet. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: His feet hit the ground quickly because he does not want to be late.
quests.explanation: Run means to move on your feet very fast. Walk is the slower way to move on your feet.
quests.funFact: When you run, both feet are in the air for a moment with every stride.

quests.instruction: Sara goes to her seat slowly, one calm step after another. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: Her feet touch the ground one at a time and there is no hurry.
quests.explanation: Walk means to move forward on your feet in steady steps. One foot stays on the ground.
quests.funFact: Most babies take their first steps around their first birthday.

quests.instruction: Leo is tired and puts his body down on a chair to rest. What does he do?
quests.hint: A chair is made for this action.
quests.explanation: Sit means to rest your body on a seat. Your weight is on your bottom, not on your feet.
quests.funFact: Sit is often the first command a puppy learns.

quests.instruction: The teacher says, 'Please get up from your chairs.' What should the class do?
quests.hint: It is the opposite of sitting down.
quests.explanation: Stand means to be on your feet with your body upright. It is the opposite of sit.
quests.funFact: Horses can even sleep while standing up.

quests.instruction: Zoe sees a puddle and pushes off the ground with both feet to get over it. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: Her feet leave the ground for a moment.
quests.explanation: Jump means to push yourself up off the ground with your legs.
quests.funFact: Frogs have strong back legs that help them jump far.

quests.instruction: Omar opens a storybook and looks at the words on the page. What is he doing?
quests.hint: The words are already on the page; someone else made them.
quests.explanation: Read means to look at words and understand what they say. Write is when you make the words yourself.
quests.funFact: The word 'read' is spelled the same way in the past, but it sounds like 'red'.

quests.instruction: Lily holds a pencil and puts her name at the top of the page. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: She is making letters appear on the paper.
quests.explanation: Write means to make letters or words on paper with a pencil or pen.
quests.funFact: Pencil marks are not ink; they are tiny bits of graphite rubbed onto the paper.

quests.instruction: Arjun uses crayons to make a picture of his house. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: He is making lines and shapes, but no brush is needed.
quests.explanation: Draw means to make a picture with lines, using a pencil, crayon or pen.
quests.funFact: Some cave drawings are many thousands of years old.

quests.instruction: The children run to the playground because they want to have fun with their friends. What will they do there?
quests.hint: Fun is the whole reason for this action.
quests.explanation: Play means to do something for fun, like a game or a sport.
quests.funFact: Puppies and kittens play too, and it helps them learn to move well.

quests.instruction: Hana opens her mouth and makes music with her voice. What is she doing?
quests.hint: The sound she makes has a tune.
quests.explanation: Sing means to make music with your voice. Talk is also with your voice, but it has no tune.
quests.funFact: Singing with others can make people feel happy and close to each other.

quests.instruction: The music starts, and Ben moves his body to the beat. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: His whole body follows the rhythm.
quests.explanation: Dance means to move your body in time with music.
quests.funFact: Almost every culture in the world has its own kind of dance.

quests.instruction: When the show ends, everyone hits their hands together to say well done. What do they do?
quests.hint: Their hands make a sound as they meet.
quests.explanation: Clap means to hit your hands together to make a sound, often to show you liked something.
quests.funFact: Clap makes a sound because the air between your hands is pushed out quickly.

quests.instruction: Kofi turns on the tap and uses soap on his dirty hands. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: He uses soap and water to make something clean.
quests.explanation: Wash means to clean something with water, and often with soap too.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands for about twenty seconds helps get rid of germs.

quests.instruction: Nina pulls the handle so she can go through the door. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: After this action, the door is no longer shut.
quests.explanation: Open means to move something so that it is not shut. A door, a box or a book can open.
quests.funFact: Many shop doors open by themselves when they sense you coming.

quests.instruction: It is getting cold, so Dad shuts the window. What does he do?
quests.hint: This is the opposite of Nina's action with the door.
quests.explanation: Close means to shut something. Close is the opposite of open.
quests.funFact: The verb 'close' sounds different when it means 'near': you stand close to a friend.

quests.instruction: Max turns his eyes toward a bird in the tree. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: He uses his eyes, not his ears or nose.
quests.explanation: Look means to turn your eyes toward something so you can see it.
quests.funFact: Your eyes blink about every few seconds without you even thinking about it.

quests.instruction: The room is quiet, and Priya wants to hear the soft music. What does she do?
quests.hint: She pays attention with her ears.
quests.explanation: Listen means to pay attention to sounds so that you can hear them well.
quests.funFact: You have two ears so your brain can tell which direction a sound is coming from.

quests.instruction: Sam puts his fingers gently on a rabbit's soft fur. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: His fingers, not his eyes, are doing the work.
quests.explanation: Touch means to put your hand or fingers on something and feel it.
quests.funFact: Your fingertips have many tiny sensors, so they feel small details very well.

quests.instruction: Mia holds out a pencil so her friend can have it. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: The pencil goes from her hand to someone else's hand.
quests.explanation: Give means to hand something to another person so that it becomes theirs.
quests.funFact: Giving a small gift is a way many families say thank you.

quests.instruction: Jay reaches up and gets the ball from the shelf. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: The ball goes from the shelf to his hand.
quests.explanation: Take means to get something and hold it or move it. Take is almost the opposite of give.
quests.funFact: 'Take care' is a friendly way to say goodbye in English.

quests.instruction: Ella sees her grandma at the window and moves her hand from side to side. What is she doing?
quests.hint: Her hand moves to say hello from far away.
quests.explanation: Wave means to move your hand from side to side to greet someone or say goodbye.
quests.funFact: In many countries, people wave to say hello or goodbye.

quests.instruction: Dev swings his leg, and the football flies across the field. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: The ball is hit with a foot.
quests.explanation: Kick means to hit something with your foot.
quests.funFact: In football, most of the game is played with the feet.

quests.instruction: Zoe lifts the ball in her hand and sends it through the air to her brother. What does she do?
quests.hint: She uses her arm, not her foot.
quests.explanation: Throw means to send something through the air with your arm and hand.
quests.funFact: Throwing a ball in a high curve can make it travel farther.

quests.instruction: Her brother puts out both hands and grabs the ball before it lands. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: He stops the ball and holds it.
quests.explanation: Catch means to stop something that is moving through the air and hold it.
quests.funFact: Catching a ball needs your eyes and hands to work together.

quests.instruction: Ali jumps into the pool and moves through the water using his arms and legs. What is he doing?
quests.hint: He moves forward, but not on the ground.
quests.explanation: Swim means to move through water by using your arms and legs.
quests.funFact: Swimming works the muscles in your arms, legs and back at the same time.

quests.instruction: Ivy puts her hands and feet on the ladder and goes up, one step at a time. Which verb fits?
quests.hint: She goes up using both hands and feet.
quests.explanation: Climb means to go up something by using your hands and feet.
quests.funFact: Going down a ladder is safest when you face the ladder.

quests.instruction: Raj sits on his bicycle and pushes the pedals around. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: He sits on something that moves, and he makes it move.
quests.explanation: Ride means to sit on something like a bike or a horse and travel on it. We usually drive a car.
quests.funFact: The first bicycles had no pedals; riders pushed along the ground with their feet.
